**1 — Scene:** A mixed plate with a bone-in cooked meat portion, two orange baked rounds, two pieces of tuna nigiri, and cucumber. The meat looks most like a braised short rib; the orange rounds appear to be savory sweet-potato biscuits, though identification is uncertain.

**2 — Vessel:** A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area: 3.14 × 13² ≈ **530 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Short-rib meat, two orange biscuits, tuna nigiri (fish and rice), and cucumber. No distinct sauce or added oil is visible. The exposed bone is excluded from edible weight.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Short-rib meat, excluding bone | 11% | 58 × 1.8 = 104 ml | 0.95 | 99 g | 290 | 287 kcal |
| Two sweet-potato biscuits | 11% | 58 × 2.4 = 139 ml | 0.90 | 125 g | 320 | 400 kcal |
| Two tuna nigiri | 8% | 42 × 1.8 = 76 ml | 0.95 | 72 g | 150 | 108 kcal |
| Cucumber pieces | 3% | 16 × 1.0 = 16 ml | 0.65 | 10 g | 15 | 2 kcal |

The edible items cover approximately **33%** of the plate; the exposed bone occupies a little additional area. Nigiri is calculated as one combined item to avoid counting overlapping fish and rice twice.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **306 g edible food and 797 kcal** is plausible for this relatively sparse plate with dense biscuits and fatty meat. The largest uncertainty is the identity and recipe of the orange rounds.
